content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any trigger-rate/hardware/project requirement documents. Extract the three allowed candidate algorithms, their Level-1 hardware deployability constraints, the allocated trigger rate definition, and the valid threshold range of 20–60 GeV."},{"id":"s2","description":"For each candidate algorithm that is deployable in the Level-1 hardware, run simulate_efficiency at a coarse threshold grid: 20, 30, 40, 50, and 60 GeV. Tabulate the returned signal efficiencies and use record_results for the numeric efficiencies and thresholds."},{"id":"s3","description":"Identify the best coarse threshold region for each viable algorithm. Around each candidate’s best coarse point, run simulate_efficiency on a finer 5 GeV grid within the allowed 20–60 GeV range, including neighboring thresholds around the coarse maximum. Record the numeric efficiencies and thresholds."},{"id":"s4","description":"Compare all simulated results across the three candidates and select the deployable algorithm/threshold pair with the highest signal efficiency at the allocated trigger rate. If two choices have indistinguishable efficiency, prefer the more robust Level-1 implementation described in the project documents, then the lower threshold."},{"id":"s5","description":"Perform one final validation simulation at the selected algorithm and threshold, confirm it satisfies the candidate_specs.md and hardware constraints, and record the final numeric threshold and signal efficiency for the reporting module’s recommendation."}]}
